summary: No findings. Untrusted input considered: a foreign same-origin IndexedDB connection (e.g. an older app build in another tab) that ignores versionchange. Path: factory.open(DB_VERSION) -> onblocked -> reject(UpgradeBlockedError) -> openHandStore clears its cached promise only if it is still the current one (db === opening), so a later call retries and other open errors stay sticky as before. Connection leak: the blocked request stays pending; when the blocker closes it runs the additive-only upgrade (create stores; v4 seeds default settings only when oldVersion < 4) and onsuccess closes the late connection without resolving, so it cannot hold the database or block the retry. A late onerror rejects an already-settled promise, which does nothing. Data loss: none. The upgrade only adds stores and never touches existing records, and a late upgrade that commits before the close leaves a correct v5 schema. Repeated retries while still blocked each queue one more pending open. These are user-driven and each closes itself once unblocked, so there is no meaningful resource exhaustion. The error message is static (no sensitive data). The opening.catch branch handles its own rejection, and callers still receive the original rejecting promise, which the existing App handlers catch. The UI/CSS changes (DOM order of the Home button, flex order) touch no trust boundary. No new dependencies.
